full_judgment: 25. It is evident that under section 5(4) in the case of suit for sale on the basis of a mortgage, as is the case in the present instance, preliminary decree shall become final upon an auction sale taking place and concomitantly the right to redemption shall be deemed to come to an end at that point in time. It is clear from the law that until such auction sale and final decree, the right to redeem remains intact. Applied in conjunction with section 33(7), however, that deeming provision of section 5(4) may very well be argued to meet its limitation in the circumstances envisaged in section 33(7) given that the fact or concept of an. auction sale does not arise in section 33(7) scenario. In that scenario the very issuance of Certificate of Title and its registration thereof may be construed by many as a finality of the Execution process, thereby, extinguishing a right of redemption at the point of such issuance. The petitioner's respond to that line of thinking by stressing that the right to redeem is in fact a legal and substantive right to property which ought not to be extinguished by mere implication given that section 33(7) remains silent on the extinguishments of the capacity to redeem existing in any mortgagor. It is pointed out that this question of redemption could also have been better understood, should section 5(4) have borne express reference to the status of a right of redemption in the context of section 33(7), But clearly section 5(4) bears no such reference to section 33(7). It is, accordingly, argued that such absence of specific declaration of the law extinguishing the right of redemption on the issuance of a section 33(7) Certificate of Title, it would be misconceived to expressly find on such extinguishments to the detriment of a mortgagor and this would go beyond the rules of either statutory interpretation or construction. This Court finds merit in these submissions as the petitioner is willing to redeem the mortgage upon satisfaction of the Bank's outstanding claims in its totality.
